newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to take two weeks off after Germany trip.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to take two weeks off after Germany trip.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will take two weeks holiday after he visits Germany from April 16 to 18, the presidential press service said on Wednesday.

A Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin would travel to the Black Sea resort of Sochi. Sidelined with heart problems and then pneumonia for most of the second half of last year and for some of this year, Yeltsin often travels to Sochi in the spring.

The Kremlin said the 66-year-old president would break off his vacation at the end of the month to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin in Moscow. Ministers will also travel to Sochi to meet Yeltsin while he is away.
"Naturally, the president will perform all the consitutional duties of the head of the state," Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.

Yeltsin has been stepping up his workload steadily since he recovered from pneumonia and has had a series of meetings with foreign leaders, including a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki last month.
He will address Russians on the radio on Thursday, dealing with the problem of corruption and on strengthening state power. The speech will be broadcast at 9 a.m. (0500 GMT).
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yeltsin as telling new First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov on Wednesday that all officials should follow the credo shared by the two men.
"You and I have the same credo -- not to take bribes", Yeltsin said.
